findings.what: No test checks that the renew screen shows an accepted renewal. The only success test is a client unit test on a made-up 201, which a stub that only echoes would pass.
findings.why: WB-5 includes 'renew inside the window'. RenewPolicy.tsx handles the success path (the 'Renewed…' answer, and `shown = renewal.value` drawing the new term last on the timeline), but no e2e or screen test reaches it. The e2e comment scopes it out. tests/web/unit/client/wb-5.test.ts:78 only checks that renewPolicy hands back the body it was served. A page.route answer of 201, the same made-up body the unit test already uses, could drive the screen. Each rule row needs a success test that a stub can't pass (reviewer check 3).

findings.what: The default-method test sells with 'Card', which is also the screen's starting value and its fallback. A screen that never reads the term's method still passes.
findings.why: Anti-oracle rule: the value a test sets must differ from what a stub or the code's default would produce. Here the test value equals the screen's starting state and its fallback (RenewPolicy.tsx:24 and :68). It never proves that the payment-method default comes from the current term. Selling with DirectDebit would.

findings.what: The request log keeps no headers and rebuilds bodies by parsing and re-stringifying them, so the page can't show the exact exchange the signed-off wb-requests reference shows.
findings.why: WB-7 asks for 'the exact request and response of every action'. docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-requests/populated.html:33 shows 'Request headers (6)' and 'Response headers (4)' inside http-exchange. LoggedExchange has no headers, and RequestLogPage.tsx gives HttpExchange none. JSON.parse also loses the API's own number formatting (100.00 becomes 100). Parity passed because it compares data-comp structure only. No wb-7 test asserts headers, so the tests need a matching addition.

findings.what: termMethod falls back to 'Card' when the term's payment isn't found or isn't recognised. The form then shows a method the API never returned.
findings.why: react-web, 'Screens are composed': a value the data doesn't hold renders as an empty or 'not built' state, never as a default (HONEST-1). The code-quality slop list also counts invented behaviour.

findings.what: A request still waiting for its answer shows in the log table with status 0 (`entry.status ?? 0`). The API never returned that status.
findings.why: HONEST-1: no number may appear that isn't in the data. A pending or unanswered exchange should look pending or unanswered, as the drawer already does with outcome 'pending'.

findings.what: unique() builds policy references from Date.now(), in wb-5.spec.ts:10 and wb-7.spec.ts:11. The test data then depends on the time of the run.
findings.why: Anti-oracle rule: no random or time-of-day data, and each test passes its own literal reference. The e2e API starts on a fresh database (web-testing, 'Running'), so a literal reference per test would be unique enough.

notes: TDD order holds: the WB-5 and WB-7 red commits (8c26d5d..75f3244) come before the greens (70dea3a, 50d3d4e). The I5 finding-red ab061ce failed at gate.finding-red before the fix e795f19, and that fix carries Fixes-Finding A1/I5.
